title: Genetic manipulation of cervical lymph node-innervating neurons in mice via viral tracing
author: Guo, Ji, et al.

steps.title: Prepare viral injection mixture
steps.instruction: Retrieve AAV aliquots from the –80 °C freezer, keep on ice, and allow them to thaw completely; use high‑titer virus (≥ 1 × 10^13 vg/mL, lower titers ≈ 5 × 10^12 vg/mL acceptable). Prepare a 0.1 % Fast Green solution, filter it through a 0.22 µm filter, and immediately mix the thawed virus with the Fast Green solution at a 3:1 (virus: dye) volume ratio in a sterile microcentrifuge tube. Keep the viral mixture on ice until injection.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve AAV from –80 °C, place on ice.
Thaw completely.
Confirm virus titer ≥ 1 × 10^13 vg/mL (or ≥ 5 × 10^12 vg/mL if acceptable).
Prepare 0.1 % Fast Green solution.
Sterilize Fast Green by passing through a 0.22 µm filter.
Mix virus and Fast Green 3:1 (virus:dye) in a sterile tube.
Keep mixture on ice until injection.

steps.title: Set up surgical instruments
steps.instruction: Cover the surgical table with a disposable drape, arrange all equipment, optionally set up a dissecting microscope, pre‑warm a heating pad to 37 °C, ensure the anesthesia system (isoflurane vaporizer or injectable mix) is functional, sterilize all surgical tools by high‑pressure steam or bead sterilizer, clean the 2.5 µL Hamilton microsyringe with 75 % ethanol followed by sterile 0.9 % saline, verify smooth plunger movement, and gather consumables (75 % ethanol, depilatory cream, sterile gauze, sterile 0.9 % saline, ophthalmic ointment, sterile cotton swabs, 4‑0 surgical sutures).

substeps.instruction: Cover table with disposable drape and arrange equipment.
Set up dissecting microscope if available.
Pre‑warm heating pad to 37 °C.
Check anesthesia system (isoflurane vaporizer or injectable mix).
Sterilize instruments by high‑pressure steam or bead sterilizer.
Clean 2.5 µL Hamilton microsyringe with 75 % ethanol then sterile 0.9 % saline.
Confirm microsyringe plunger moves smoothly and is unclogged.
Prepare consumables: 75 % ethanol, depilatory cream, sterile gauze, sterile 0.9 % saline, ophthalmic ointment, sterile cotton swabs, 4‑0 sutures.

steps.title: Anesthetize mouse and prep site
steps.instruction: Select a healthy C57BL/6 mouse (4–6 weeks old) and weigh it to calculate anesthetic dose. Induce anesthesia either with isoflurane (3 %–4 % in induction chamber at 0.8–1 L/min, then maintain 1.5 %–2 % via nose cone) or with sodium pentobarbital (1 % solution, 30–50 mg/kg; inject into lower abdominal quadrant after disinfecting with 75 % ethanol and confirming no blood return). After the anesthetic takes effect, verify depth by lack of hind‑paw withdrawal. Apply ophthalmic ointment, place mouse supine on the heating pad, secure limbs with tape, shave the submandibular region to the neck root, apply depilatory cream for 1–2 min, wipe clean with wet gauze, and disinfect the area with povidone‑iodine followed by 75 % ethanol.

substeps.instruction: Select healthy C57BL/6 mouse, 4–6 weeks old; weigh mouse.
Induce anesthesia:
Isoflurane: place mouse in induction chamber with 3 %–4 % isoflurane (0.8–1 L/min); once recumbent, maintain 1.5 %–2 % via nose cone.
Or sodium pentobarbital: disinfect lower abdomen with 75 % ethanol, insert needle into lower abdominal quadrant, aspirate to confirm no blood/urine, inject 1 % pentobarbital sodium at 30–50 mg/kg.
Wait for full anesthetic effect; verify depth by pinching hind paw (no withdrawal).
Apply ophthalmic ointment to eyes.
Place mouse supine on heating pad (37 °C).
Secure limbs with tape if needed.
Shave fur from submandibular region to neck root.
Apply depilatory cream for 1–2 min, then wipe with wet gauze.
Disinfect surgical site with povidone‑iodine then 75 % ethanol.

description: The nervous system is a critical player in inter-organ immune regulation, and lymph nodes (LNs) are known to be innervated by sensory neurons with immunomodulatory potential.2 In the context of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), the crosstalk between tumor-innervating nociceptive neurons and cervical tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLNs) plays a pivotal role in remodeling the immune microenvironment. However, precisely manipulating these specific LN-innervating neurons without affecting the entire peripheral nervous system remains a technical challenge. Here, we present a protocol for the specific genetic manipulation of cervical LN-innervating nociceptive neurons in mice. Following the microinjecting retrograde adeno-associated viruses (AAV2/retro) directly into the cervical LNs, the virus undergoes retrograde transport to the neuronal cell bodies located in the trigeminal ganglia (TG). This approach allows for the specific labeling (e.g., using hSyn-EGFP), chemogenetic inhibition (e.g., using hM4D(Gi)-mCherry), or gene knockout (e.g., utilizing Cre-loxP systems) of these neurons to functionally dissect neuroimmune circuits. The protocol below describes the specific steps for using C57BL/6 mice. However, we have also used this protocol in genetically engineered strains, such as Calcaflox/flox and Scn10aCatCh-EYFP mice. The total hands-on time for the surgical procedure is approximately 60 min per mouse for an experienced researcher.
